question: Could one-pass training-only continuous embedding noise be a supported next native Base comparison under the unchanged quality and resource gates?

primary_sources.commit_observation: git ls-remote HEAD returned this commit; pinned README then opened and checked
primary_sources.summary: Training adds scaled uniform embedding noise. Authors report degradation without repetition penalty and recommend greedy decoding with penalty1.2. Limited instruction-finetuning evidence does not establish our Japanese10M Base effect.

Main models are billions of parameters and instruction-finetuned. Generation comparisons use repetition penalty1.2 throughout, including varied decoding settings. Observed conversational improvements cannot be transferred directly to native Japanese10M Base.

comparison_to_prior: Continuous additive input-embedding noise differs from existing inverted p.1 embedding/residual dropout and two-view RDrop; difference alone is not efficacy or exhaustive novelty evidence. No implementation absence claim from keyword search. Closed dropout100M remains rejected; RDrop remains cost-closed.

decision.inference: Insufficient fit for this next comparison, not proof NEFTune fails on10M or a permanent prohibition if genuinely new evidence appears.
decision.reason: Available primary evidence does not adequately support native raw-generation improvement without decoding changes in this project, and no measured new technical/science feasibility exists. Avoid spending the last technical seconds on an unsupported cheaper-looking regularizer.

next_action: No further automatic regularizer sweep or synthetic scaffolding. Preserve fit rejection and audit the original completion requirements/resource prerequisites. No claim that every possible intervention is ruled out.
